moments.text: We agree the questions with you, or with your investors.
moments.label: Questions

moments.text: Read access to code, cloud and documents, and interviews with your team are booked.
moments.label: Access

moments.text: Architecture, data and delivery are reviewed, with the costs and risks priced.
moments.label: Review

moments.text: Findings are checked with your engineers, so nothing in the report is a surprise.
moments.label: Check

moments.text: A written report: the red flags, what they cost to fix and a 90-day plan, then a read-out.
moments.label: Report

moments.text: We agree what the first 40 hours should answer.
moments.label: Questions

moments.text: Read-only access to your AWS accounts and diagrams.
moments.label: Access

moments.text: An architecture review: what holds, what will not, and what it costs to change.
moments.label: Review

moments.text: Decision records for the open choices, ready for your team to sign off.
moments.label: Decisions

moments.text: A roadmap you can act on. Draw down the next block only if you need it.
moments.label: Roadmap

moments.text: We pick the use case together and agree what a good answer looks like.
moments.label: Use case

moments.text: A test set of real questions from your team, to score every version against.
moments.label: Test set

moments.text: Access to your AWS account and data. The first prototype runs on your own documents.
moments.label: Prototype

moments.text: The first version answers in staging, scored against the test set.
moments.label: Staging

moments.text: Connected to your systems, with guardrails on and the running cost measured.
moments.label: Connected

moments.text: Live for the first users, with a trace behind every answer.
moments.label: Live

moments.text: Code, evaluations and runbooks handed to your team.
moments.label: Handed off

label: SOC 2 readiness
length: 6–12 months to a Type II report

moments.text: We agree what is in scope and which criteria apply. Security always does.
moments.label: Scope

moments.text: A gap list in priority order, and a first draft of your system description.
moments.label: Gap list

moments.text: We start in your AWS accounts and tools, next to the people who will own the controls.
moments.label: In your tools

moments.text: Policies written, controls on your landing zone, and evidence collected automatically.
moments.label: Controls

moments.text: A mock audit, tested the way an auditor would. We close what is left and shortlist auditors.
moments.label: Mock audit

moments.text: Type I: an independent auditor checks the design of your controls on one date.
moments.label: Type I

moments.text: The Type II window opens. Your team runs the controls, and we check in every month.
moments.label: Window opens

moments.text: The window closes. The auditor tests it and issues your Type II report.
moments.label: Type II

moments.text: We agree the goals, the shape of the team and how we work with yours.
moments.label: Goals

moments.text: Our people join your stand-ups, your repositories and your on-call rota.
moments.label: Joined

moments.text: The first releases from the joint team reach your users.
moments.label: First release

moments.text: A review together: grow the team, shrink it, or keep it as it is.
moments.label: Review

moments.text: What we know has moved to your own people, and we step out.
moments.label: Step out
